title: The assistant that got worse
scenario: An internal policy assistant launched nine months ago with strong reviews. It answers HR and compliance questions over 40,000 documents using dense retrieval with top-k of 5, no reranker, and 256-token chunks with no overlap. Nothing in the stack has changed since launch: same model version, same prompt, same index configuration. Over the last quarter, satisfaction has fallen steadily. Spot checks find three distinct problems: answers that cite a 2023 policy superseded in 2025; answers that are fluent and confident but contain a claim absent from the retrieved passages; and answers that stop halfway through a multi-step procedure.

questions.stem: Which problem does the 256-token, no-overlap chunking most directly explain?
choices: Answers that stop halfway through a multi-step procedure
Claims absent from the retrieved passages
The overall decline in satisfaction over time
questions.explanation: Fixed-size chunking with no overlap severs documents at arbitrary boundaries, so a procedure spanning more than 256 tokens is split and only part is retrieved. The truncated-procedure symptom maps to segmentation. Stale citations are a governance problem and ungrounded claims are a grounding problem, neither caused by chunk size.

questions.stem: What is the most reliable fix for answers citing the superseded 2023 policy?
choices: Add a reranker so the newer document outranks the older one
Attach effective-date and status metadata at ingestion, filter on it at query time, and tombstone or remove superseded documents
Instruct the model in the system prompt to prefer the most recent source
Re-embed the corpus with a newer embedding model
questions.explanation: Recency is not something a relevance model can infer from text — a superseded policy is often the more semantically relevant document. Versioned metadata with query-time filtering plus an explicit retirement process makes the guarantee deterministic. Rerankers and prompts both optimize for relevance, and re-embedding changes nothing about which version exists.

questions.stem: Which metric would have caught the ungrounded-claim problem on production traffic without labeled answers?
questions.explanation: Faithfulness compares the answer's claims against the retrieved context and needs no ground truth, so it can run continuously on live traffic. Context recall requires a reference answer, exact match requires labels, and perplexity measures nothing about grounding.

questions.stem: The stack is frozen, yet quality declined steadily. What is the underlying cause?
choices: Gradual corruption of the served model weights
Drift: the questions users ask and the corpus itself both moved away from what the pipeline and its evaluation set were designed for
KV cache fragmentation accumulating over nine months
The embedding model degrading with index size
questions.explanation: With everything pinned, the environment is what changed: new policies, new vocabulary, new question types. This is why production agents need scheduled re-evaluation against refreshed data and monitoring of the input distribution, not just a launch-time evaluation. Served weights do not decay and cache behavior does not affect correctness.
